prompt.context: Our client is the CFO of a large multi-billion dollar consumer goods company in North America. The recent economic crisis has generated a need to drastically reduce costs in order to maintain the firm's future competitiveness. The senior executive team has come up with a cost reduction goal of $500 million by 2012. Since the company expects to grow its sales over the period, it has been determined that core activities such as production plans, sales, and marketing should not be affected or touched by this initiative.
prompt.question: The CFO, who is responsible for the initiative, has approached our firm to: (1) develop a comprehensive understanding of cost reduction alternatives, (2) provide a recommendation on the appropriate approach and steps to execute this initiative, and (3) provide input on who should be involved in this initiative.

clarifying_info.q: Are there any specific cost areas already identified as targets?
clarifying_info.a: No specific areas have been pre-identified; the initiative is open to all non-core cost areas.

clarifying_info.q: What is the timeline for achieving the $500 million savings?
clarifying_info.a: The goal is to achieve $500 million in cost savings by 2012.

clarifying_info.q: Are divestitures or business unit closures on the table?
clarifying_info.a: Not specified; focus should be on operational cost reduction without affecting core activities.

clarifying_info.q: Is there a budget or resource constraint for the initiative itself?
clarifying_info.a: No specific budget constraint has been mentioned for the initiative.

framework: 1. Identify cost reduction opportunities across non-core functions (categorize by lever: productivity, technology, location, outsourcing, consolidation, org structure, procurement)
2. Size each opportunity to understand which levers can contribute meaningfully toward the $500M target
3. Define the approach and implementation steps (team formation, benchmarking, implementation cycle)
4. Determine stakeholder involvement (functional experts, management, internal/external customers)
5. Synthesize into a prioritized recommendation with phasing (quick wins vs. larger transformational efforts)

questions.prompt: What are the potential cost reduction opportunities available to the client?
questions.guidance: Candidate should brainstorm broadly across non-core cost categories. Strong answers cover: workload imbalances and direct productivity improvement; technology to reduce manual work; offshoring/nearshoring selected back-office functions (accounting, finance); outsourcing non-core operations (call centers, transactional processing); consolidating office locations to reduce fixed costs; eliminating excessive organizational layers; eliminating low added-value work; supplier consolidation to reduce COGS. Candidate should note that since production, sales, and marketing are off-limits, the focus is on G&A, support functions, and procurement.

questions.prompt: What is the appropriate approach and steps the client should follow to execute this initiative?
questions.guidance: A strong answer mirrors an Organizational Change / Six Sigma model: (1) Form a dedicated cross-functional team; (2) Create incentives to promote results and collaboration; (3) Understand and inventory opportunities — list, size, and gather data; (4) Benchmark against industry peers and comparable initiatives; (5) Restore areas that are underperforming relative to design; (6) Eliminate or redesign areas that perform as designed but still have opportunity; (7) Implement, adjust, and correct iteratively.

questions.prompt: Who should be involved in this cost reduction initiative?
questions.guidance: Key stakeholders: functional/subject matter experts from impacted areas; support and visible commitment from upper management (critical for change management); internal customers (business units affected by changes); external customers where relevant (suppliers for procurement consolidation, consumers if service levels are impacted); functional areas that will be changed or disrupted.

brainstorming.prompt: Generate as many cost reduction ideas as possible across all non-core areas of the business.

categories.name: Organizational Structure
ideas: Eliminate excessive organizational layers
Remove low added-value roles and work
Balance workloads to address staffing imbalances
Consolidate duplicative functions across business units

categories.name: Technology & Automation
ideas: Implement workflow automation to reduce manual processing
Invest in ERP upgrades to eliminate redundant data entry
Use digital self-service tools to reduce support headcount
Automate reporting and compliance processes

categories.name: Location & Real Estate
ideas: Consolidate office locations to reduce fixed occupancy costs
Move back-office functions to lower-cost domestic locations
Explore nearshoring for selected finance and accounting operations

categories.name: Outsourcing
ideas: Outsource call center and customer service operations
Outsource transactional finance/accounting work (AP, AR, payroll)
Outsource IT infrastructure and helpdesk support
Outsource HR administrative functions

categories.name: Procurement & Supply Chain
ideas: Consolidate supplier base to achieve better pricing leverage
Renegotiate contracts with key vendors
Standardize specifications to reduce SKU complexity
Implement strategic sourcing across categories

categories.name: Offshoring
ideas: Move finance and accounting operations to low-cost locations (e.g., India, Eastern Europe)
Offshore IT development and maintenance
Create shared service centers in low-cost regions

recommendation: Phase 1 (Quick Wins): Target organizational restructuring — reduce layers, eliminate low added-value work, and balance workloads. These changes can be executed quickly with limited capital investment, though alone they are unlikely to yield $500M.

Phase 2 (Transformational): Pursue higher-impact levers including offshoring/outsourcing back-office functions, implementing automation technology, consolidating office locations, and executing a supplier consolidation program to reduce COGS. These efforts require more planning but carry larger dollar value.

Together, a multi-lever approach combining organizational efficiency, technology, location strategy, outsourcing, and procurement consolidation is required to credibly achieve the $500M target by 2012.
risks: Change management resistance from employees affected by outsourcing or offshoring
Service quality degradation if outsourced functions are not properly transitioned
One-time transition costs may reduce near-term savings
Management distraction from executing cost cuts while growing the business simultaneously
next_steps: Form a dedicated program management team with C-suite sponsorship
Size each opportunity category in detail and build a business case
Benchmark savings estimates against industry comparables
Develop a phased implementation roadmap with milestones and accountability owners
Establish incentive structures to drive cross-functional collaboration
